## Summary

Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd., trading internationally as Foxconn, was founded by Terry Gou on 20 February 1974 and is headquartered in Tucheng District, New Taipei City, Taiwan [2]. It builds electronics under contract for Apple (iPhone, iPad, iPod), Sony (most PlayStation consoles), Nintendo, Microsoft (Xbox), Amazon (Kindle), Google (Pixel), Xiaomi, Cisco and others, and also makes connectors, printed circuit boards and computer hardware [2]. The registry lists 129 MA-L blocks under this exact spelling at a Chongqing address, plus further blocks under other spellings at Shenzhen, Nanning, Tucheng and Hsinchu addresses [1].

Because Hon Hai is a contract manufacturer, a MAC in its blocks is a device or module it built, and the brand on the box is usually someone else's. One documented case is a Foxconn T77H348.02 laptop Wi-Fi card, sold on eBay as an Atheros AR9462 (AR5B22) with Bluetooth 4.0, which a forum poster bought and planned to fit in a ThinkPad X200 [3]; that is a single seller-reported part, so silicon and radios are inferred, not general.

Parent company is left unknown because the source consulted names none; it lists Hon Hai as a public company traded in Taipei and London [2]. The FCC grantee code is not listed because the FCC ID databases and the module wikis (fccid.io, fcc.report, TechInfoDepot) refused this session's requests. Randomization depends on the operating system of the product Hon Hai built, and no source in hand documents it, so it is unknown. No security advisory naming Hon Hai as the vendor of a networked device was found.
